question: Which import goods had the largest declines in value between 2018 and 2019 during the COVID-19 crisis in Luxembourg?

limitations.message: Values are in current euros (nominal), not adjusted for price changes.
3.8 % of this value is confidential at full product detail (masked codes); it is shown as a separate 'Confidential' slice, never dropped.

sql:
SELECT
  year,
  hs2 AS key,
  flow,
  SUM(value_eur) AS value_eur,
  SUM(qty_kg) AS qty_kg
FROM v_lu_trade_hs2
WHERE
  period >= CAST('2018-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND period < CAST('2020-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND flow = 'import'
  AND year IN (2018, 2019)
GROUP BY
  year,
  key,
  flow
ORDER BY
  year,
  value_eur DESC
LIMIT 10000
title: Largest changes by product group — imports 2018–2019

insight: The import goods with the largest declines in value between 2018 and 2019 in Luxembourg were Optical, measuring and medical instruments, which fell by 315.9 million euros to 339.1 million euros.
Overall, imports of Optical, measuring and medical instruments decreased by 48.2 percent, the largest percentage drop among the listed goods.
Other notable declines were in Iron and steel, down by 189.8 million euros to 1.16 billion euros, and Inorganic chemicals and related compounds, down by 65.0 million euros to 161.2 million euros.
In contrast, imports of Electrical machinery and equipment increased by 1.10 billion euros to 2.58 billion euros during the same period.
The data are in current euros and do not account for price changes, and 3.8 percent of the import values are confidential and not detailed.
